newsitem.title: INDIA: India says pension, insurance reforms needed.
newsitem.headline: India says pension, insurance reforms needed.

text.p: India's annual Economic Survey said on Tuesday that there is a need to reform pension funds and insurance companies to woo private capital into the infrastructure sector.

"There is also a need to introduce approriate reforms in public provident funds, pension funds and insurance companies so that the private sector can have access to these funds for infrastructure development," it said.

The survey said a slowdown in telecommunications growth "suggests that the pace of implementation of telecommunication reform needs to be accelerated and its scope widened to include Deparment of Telecommunications as a service provider".
The government said to mobilise long-term finance, domestic capital markets have to be reformed to create a vibrant bond market.
The survey urged acclerated growth of infrastructure industries like power, road, ports, telecommunication and avaition to sustain a long-term annual economic growth of seven percent.
"We must quickly resolve the residual difficulties in the induction of private providers of basic and cellular telecom services," the government said.
The survey also urged for resolving policy "ambiguities" relating to the aviation industry.
